text:
marcos: heads-up — since ~03:20 UTC we're seeing a spike (~10-15%) of small GPU pods stuck in Pending in us-west-2a even though cluster shows free GPU capacity in other AZs. Scheduler logs show '0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu' but `kubectl get nodes -o json` shows available GPUs on some nodes. Anyone seeing this?

li-wei: same here. These are the tiny inference pods (request: 0.25 GPU, cpu: 1) hitting the predicate mismatch. Looks like fragmentation: nodes have 1 full GPU or a full MIG partition so scheduler thinks no fit.

marcos: exact error from one pod describe: ```Events:
  Type     Reason              Age                 From               Message
  ----     ------              ----                ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling    2m (x5 over 4m)     default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu```

ops_sre: quick check — cluster-autoscaler did not scale up because the scale-up candidates are filtered by taint 'net-bandwidth-low' we added to the bw-optimized pool in us-west-2a. CA saw potential capacity but filtered them out as they aren't allowed for these pods. Investigating if taint should be removed for small-gpu workloads.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: nodepool/gpu-bw-optimized created by infra-cfg 6h ago in us-west-2a (taints: net-bandwidth-low=true:NoSchedule, labels: gpu.profile=bw-optimized).

tasha: notable config: pods include nodeSelector: gpu.profile=shared and a topologySpreadConstraint across AZs. Small pods prefer shared nodes but the new nodepool is labeled bw-optimized only. Combined with the spread constraint scheduler rejects mixing.

li-wei: here's a trimmed kube-scheduler log (v=4) entry that looks relevant: ```I0318 03:21:12.345678 1 predicates.go:211] PodFitsResources failed for pod "tiny-inf" on node "node-az2a-07": insufficient resources: requested 0.25 nvidia.com/gpu, available 0.0 (nonzero but not allocatable due to MIG config)```

gavin: short-term ideas: 1) remove the net-bandwidth-low taint from gpu-bw-optimized so CA will consider them; 2) set CA expander to 'least-waste' so it prefers node types that avoid fractional leftover; 3) add a scheduler plugin/priority to prefer packing fractional requests together (reduce fragmentation).

ops_sre: I'm +1 on removing taint temporarily while we validate bandwidth perf. I'll patch the nodepool in staging first.

marcos: another quick workaround is to add a node label 'gpu.slice=small' on a subset of nodes and update tiny pods' nodeAffinity to prefer that. That way we can co-locate similar request shapes and avoid cross-contaminating full-GPU nodes.

tasha: I'll prepare a canary: add label to 2 nodes in staging, update deployment nodeAffinity, and flip CA expander to least-waste in staging. If green, promote to prod later today.

li-wei: also recommend we capture a few packing snapshots and run our binpacking sim (binpack-sim) with current pod mix to measure fragmentation impact. I'll run that and post numbers.

marcos: plan:
- ops_sre: remove net-bandwidth-low taint from 1 nodepool in staging (ops_sre)
- tasha: add gpu.slice=small label and patch affinity in staging (tasha)
- li-wei: collect scheduler traces and run binpack-sim (li-wei)
- gavin: test CA expander tweak in staging and measure scale-up choices (gavin)

marcos: revisit here in 30m. If anyone finds a blocker or rollback reason post here. :thumbsup:

ops_sre: done in staging, removing taint now — monitoring pods.

infra-bot: alert: 03:42 UTC 10 pods transitioned from Pending->Running in staging after taint removal.

gavin: initial binpack-sim numbers show fragmentation reduced by ~35% when using affinity+least-waste instead of default. Will push a short PR with config changes for review.

marcos: great. If staging holds we can roll to prod off-hours. Thanks all.
